nodes.description: Root node representing the individual in therapy.
Patient's age, gender, cultural background, education, vocation, and social context.
Diagnoses, symptom types, severity, and progression (including Axis I/II and multi-axial information).
Initial complaints and ongoing or new issues as identified across sessions.
Historical antecedents including childhood, formative experiences, major life events, trauma, and social/family/educational/vocational history.
Central beliefs, thinking and behavioral patterns, evolving case conceptualization, and theoretical understanding (schemas, thought patterns).
Central beliefs about self, others, and world (e.g., incompetence, unlovability), including their developmental origins and conviction strength.
Attitudes, rules, and assumptions derived from core beliefs.
Recurring faulty patterns of thinking (e.g., catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking) linked to automatic thoughts or beliefs.
Recurring, spontaneous thoughts in response to situations, including emotional and behavioral reactions.
Patterns and vocabulary of emotional reactivity, intensity ratings, dysfunctional emotion-related beliefs, and changes over time.
Typical activities, routines, avoidance/approach behaviors, and mastery/pleasurable activities including changes since symptom onset.
Adaptive and maladaptive strategies, historical and current use, compensatory behaviors, and progress in coping skills.
Assets, sources of resilience, and progress in skill autonomy (becoming one's own therapist).
Quality, ruptures, repairs, feedback history, and collaboration history with this and former clinicians.
Patient’s goal list, both ongoing and new, with behavioral specifications and evolution across sessions.
Interventions used, responses, effectiveness, rationale, and patient preferences (e.g., coping cards, behavioral experiments, imagery, bibliotherapy).
Assignment types/completion, adherence patterns, outcomes, barriers encountered, self-efficacy changes, self-therapy practices.
Patterns and records of activity scheduling, mastery/pleasure ratings, progress, and data from activity charts.
Design, predicted outcomes, actual results, reflection on dysfunctional cognitions, and role in belief modification.
Strategies taught/implemented, booster session content/outcomes, patient’s readiness and plans for maintaining gains.
Individual problem-solving style, progress on graded tasks/exposure, and responses to setbacks/relapses.
Composition, quality, and utilization of external support systems.
Therapist’s notes regarding their own reactions, assumptions, and skill development regarding the patient and therapy process.
